_doc: Category 25 (Cannabis, Hemp, and CBD Products) HMTc standard compiler config. Method v2.0, government-limit default, ROUTE-PRESERVING. For each (subcategory, analyte) the config names EXPLICITLY the applicable sovereign cannabis maximums as a set of register-row ids; the compiler takes the strictest (min) as the HMTc value (a lookup, never an occurrence percentile). The applicable pool for a row is the route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules (MA all-uses, Nevada, Israel) plus that row's own route-specific rules (California inhalable/non-inhalable, Colorado inhaled/oral/topical, Maryland inhalation/oral/cutaneous/edible, MA ingestion-only). An inhalation-route limit is NEVER applied to an ingested or topical product, and vice-versa; where a stricter cannabis limit exists but belongs to a different route it is listed in audit_excluded_ids with a documented reason and the compiler's verify pass confirms every stricter-unselected cannabis row is either applied or so acknowledged. Vape hardware is intentionally NOT compiled: its governing quantity is metal RELEASE into inhaled aerosol, not total product content, and the aerosol-release test architecture is a reserved governance decision (see reserved below and docs/governance/category-25-step0-lock.md). Numeric outputs are STAFF/HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19).
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, route-preserving; strictest applicable sovereign cannabis maximum; occurrence never selects a value)

iAs.control: Cannabis programs set arsenic limits without speciation; these are recorded and certified as total arsenic. Total As is measured on every lot and bounds the inorganic fraction; any elevated total-As result triggers iAs speciation.
iAs.reference_method: Total As by ICP-MS; inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS on an elevated total-As result.

MeHg.control: Cannabis has no methylmercury bioaccumulation pathway. Total Hg is measured on every lot and bounds the methylmercury fraction; there is no route by which a certified cannabis product accumulates MeHg above the total-Hg limit.
MeHg.reference_method: Total Hg by EPA 7473 or ICP-MS; reflex MeHg speciation only on an anomalous total-Hg result.

Ni.control: Nickel is a mandatory total-panel result because cannabis accumulates Ni from soil and inhalation hardware can release it, but no loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a finished-product total-Ni maximum. Report every result, investigate source and route, and do not represent this cell as a numeric government limit.
Ni.reference_method: Total Ni by ICP-MS; for inhaled products, aerosol-emissions testing separates plant/extract contamination from hardware release.

Sn.control: No loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a total-tin maximum. Total Sn remains mandatory surveillance, with any quantifiable result investigated for packaging, solder, catalyst, or device contact.
Sn.reference_method: Total Sn by ICP-MS; organotin speciation when the formulation, elastomer, catalyst, or packaging pathway makes organotin plausible.

Al.control: No loaded sovereign cannabis rule sets a total-aluminium maximum. Total Al remains mandatory surveillance and elevated results trigger soil, processing-aid, excipient, or device-source investigation.
Al.reference_method: Total Al by ICP-MS with route-appropriate blank and device controls.

Cr-VI.control: Total chromium is measured on every lot. Inhaled products and any anomalous total-Cr result require Cr(VI) speciation; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) by validated species-specific IC-ICP-MS with matrix-specific recovery controls.

cannabis-vape-hardware.name: Vape cartridges and hardware
cannabis-vape-hardware.reason: The governing quantity for vape hardware is metal RELEASE into inhaled aerosol (coil/heating-element leaching of Pb, Ni, and Cr), not total product content. A total-content ug/kg limit would misrepresent the hazard basis. The aerosol-release test architecture — and whether hardware is factored per-category here or under one shared inhalable-hardware treatment shared with nicotine vapes — is a reserved governance decision for Karen (docs/governance/taxonomy-reorganization-2026-06.md section 4; category-25-step0-lock.md). No numeric standard is set until that architecture is locked.
cannabis-vape-hardware.governing_basis_when_unreserved: aerosol-emissions basis (mass emitted per puff or per gram aerosolized), not product-content ug/kg; Pb/Ni/Cr from the heating element are the primary analytes.

cannabis-flower.name: Cannabis flower and dried herb
cannabis-flower.route_basis_label: finished inhalable cannabis, product-as-tested (as sold); no reconstitution
cannabis-flower.scope_note: Inhaled route. Applicable pool = route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules plus inhalation-specific rules (California inhalable, Colorado inhaled/nasal, Maryland inhalation). Non-inhaled route limits are not applied.

Cr.note: Maryland is the only sovereign cannabis program that sets a total-chromium action limit; its inhalation-route value governs the inhaled flower row directly.

cannabis-edibles.name: Cannabis edibles
cannabis-edibles.route_basis_label: finished edible cannabis product, as sold (product-as-tested); no reconstitution
cannabis-edibles.scope_note: Ingested food-form route. Applicable pool = route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules plus ingestion-specific rules (California non-inhalable, Colorado oral, MA ingestion-only, Maryland edible). Inhalation-route limits are not applied (see audit_excluded_ids).
cannabis-edibles.route_exclusion_reason: inhalation-route sovereign limit; not applicable to an ingested edible product

Cr.control: No protective sovereign cannabis chromium maximum applies to edibles. Maryland omits chromium from its edible-cannabis row entirely, and its oral-route total-chromium action level (1,100,000 ug/kg, a back-calculation from the USP <232> oral chromium PDE at an assumed serving mass) is non-protective and is not adopted as a numeric certification limit. Total Cr is measured on every lot; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) speciation by IC-ICP-MS on any anomalous total-Cr result.

cannabis-tinctures-oils.name: Cannabis tinctures and sublingual oils
cannabis-tinctures-oils.route_basis_label: finished oral/sublingual cannabis liquid, as sold (product-as-tested); no reconstitution
cannabis-tinctures-oils.scope_note: Oral/sublingual route (not a food 'edible' form). Applicable pool = route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules plus oral-route rules (California non-inhalable, Colorado oral, MA ingestion-only, Maryland oral). Inhalation-route limits are not applied (see audit_excluded_ids).
cannabis-tinctures-oils.route_exclusion_reason: inhalation-route sovereign limit; not applicable to an orally/sublingually administered product

Cr.control: No protective sovereign cannabis chromium maximum applies to oral/sublingual liquids. Maryland's oral-route total-chromium action level (1,100,000 ug/kg, a back-calculation from the USP <232> oral chromium PDE at an assumed serving mass) is non-protective and is not adopted as a numeric certification limit. Total Cr is measured on every lot; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) speciation by IC-ICP-MS on any anomalous total-Cr result.

cannabis-topicals.name: Cannabis topicals
cannabis-topicals.route_basis_label: finished topical/transdermal cannabis product, as sold (product-as-tested); no reconstitution
cannabis-topicals.scope_note: Cutaneous/dermal route. Applicable pool = route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules plus dermal rules (California non-inhalable, Colorado topical/transdermal, Maryland cutaneous). Inhalation-route limits are not applied (see audit_excluded_ids); MA ingestion-only does not apply to a topical.
cannabis-topicals.route_exclusion_reason: inhalation-route sovereign limit; not applicable to a topically applied product

Cr.control: No protective sovereign cannabis chromium maximum applies to topicals. Maryland's cutaneous-route total-chromium action level (1,100,000 ug/kg, a back-calculation from the USP <232> topical/oral chromium PDE at an assumed application mass) is non-protective and is not adopted as a numeric certification limit. Total Cr is measured on every lot; any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails certification.
Cr.reference_method: Total Cr by ICP-MS; Cr(VI) speciation by IC-ICP-MS on any anomalous total-Cr result.

cannabis-concentrates.name: Cannabis concentrates and extracts
cannabis-concentrates.route_basis_label: finished cannabis concentrate/extract, as sold (product-as-tested); no reconstitution
cannabis-concentrates.scope_note: Concentrates span more than one route of use. The row is certified on the route-agnostic all-uses cannabis rules only (MA all-uses, Nevada, Israel), plus Maryland's inhalation total-chromium value as a route-protective disclosed read-across (a concentrate may be inhaled). A concentrate marketed exclusively for a single route must additionally satisfy that route's own row.
cannabis-concentrates.route_exclusion_reason: route-specific sovereign limit; concentrates are certified on the route-agnostic all-uses basis, so route-specific stricter limits are not applied to this multi-route row (a single-route concentrate must also meet that route's row)

read_across.label: route-protective read-across from Maryland's inhalation total-chromium action limit; a concentrate may be inhaled, so the strict inhalation chromium value governs this multi-route row rather than the non-protective oral/cutaneous value
